name: Head elevation while sleeping
lead: Head elevation while sleeping means raising the upper body or head end of the bed, with pillows, a wedge or raised bed legs, so the head rests higher than the heart. In looksmaxxing communities it is used with the aim of reducing morning facial puffiness and under-eye swelling.

A general reference on periorbital puffiness says puffiness is most noticeable just after waking, likely because fluid shifts toward the face when lying flat, and that raising the head while sleeping may limit this shift.[1] No controlled study cited here has measured the effect of sleeping elevated on facial appearance.
infobox: Extra pillows, wedge, raised bed head

paras: The practice involves a modest incline during sleep rather than a change in diet or products. Positional therapy more broadly is also used in sleep medicine: more than half of people with obstructive sleep apnea have symptoms that worsen on the back, and side sleeping is a recognised option for them.[2]

The explanation given is gravitational: lying flat lets fluid redistribute toward the face overnight, and an incline is said to reduce that pooling.[1] The same reference lists salt intake, pregnancy and menstrual hormonal changes as other contributors to fluid retention around the eyes.[1]

Side sleeping and back sleeping are discussed in sleep-apnea references in connection with breathing, not appearance.[2] Some looksmaxxing discussion also raises concern that sleeping on one side may press on the face; this is not examined in the sources reviewed here.
No studies found on head elevation and facial or periorbital puffiness. Sleep-medicine references discuss sleep position for apnea but not for cosmetic outcomes.[2]

lore.intro: Head elevation is among the low-cost sleep tweaks discussed for morning puffiness.

claims.claim: Sleeping with the head raised reduces morning face and eye puffiness
claims.believers: Proponents say fluid pools in the face when flat and that an incline prevents it, with some reporting a visible difference on waking.
claims.experts: A general reference states that raising the head may limit the fluid shift behind morning swelling; no trials have measured it.[1]

card.summary: Sleeping propped up to curb morning puffiness; plausible mechanism, no trials on looks.
card.note: Evidence is limited to general descriptions; no appearance studies.

quick.overview:
Sleeping with the head raised is a no-cost practice aimed at less morning facial swelling.

References describe fluid shifting to the face when lying flat, but no study has measured whether sleeping elevated changes appearance.
quick.mechanism: Raising the head is said to reduce overnight fluid pooling around the face and eyes.
quick.risks: No specific harms are documented in the sources reviewed. Sleep position is also discussed in sleep apnea care.
